title: Bill Evans in the Mingus band and one-chord comping
summary: Evans filling in on a Bethlehem date, learning to vary voicings on one chord, and comparison with Ellington and John Lewis.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Well, after his ex-pause out there (inaudible) the kind of Blue record was really cause expose it to Bill, was the fact that Bill could do that very well, and was into all the modes and all that business of the scales.

(Inaudible) He wasn't into it until he came into my band. Just my band, Bill was a great reader and has full of knowledge is a great man with harmony. I remember the first record, the piano player didn't show up,

so I called Bill, an emergency, and he was asking all about it. I said, 'Well, you can play any kind of passing fancy chords you want, long as it has a pedal on this chord here.' (inaudible). That was for Bethlehem Records. It was (singing), Hello, Mom. I don't remember the names of them, but there was talking on the record. You remember that one?

"Every Time I Come Downtown," that one, "" and Celia, Celia was the one that had the one chord. Of course Bill could do it, because he's a thorough musician. But it took some explaining to get him to do it.

Because he wanted to go home. See, he didn't want to do anything I wouldn't like. I said, 'Well, so man, you got one chord, doesn't mean you play one chord with the same voicing every time. I said, 'Use the passing chords.' He was (inaudible) said, 'Why don't you write it out for me?' I said, 'It will take you years to write that out.' I said, at Duke; 'Look, when he plays the blues, he plays a different set on every chord change -- on every blues sequence.' He said, 'I haven't heard Duke "" you listen Gonzales, you'll hear (inaudible) do that. So he was behind Paul Gonzalez (inaudible), because he would do something different every 12 bars, him do that, when he comped, man, and never repeat himself. And Bud Powell can do that Duke is very underrated, (inaudible) man.
Oh, was it pianos? as a pianist? Yes, I agree with that.
Especially (inaudible). as a comer, to feed you. John Lewis is a good comer.
The records with Bird. He was just superb on those.
